symbols.name: B
symbols.role: outcome envelope, normalized to contain the binary support \(\{0,1\}\)

symbols.name: P
symbols.type: probability law \(P\) on the space of \(O\)

symbols.name: dBL
symbols.type: metric \(d_{\mathrm{BL}}\) on probability laws over bounded Euclidean spaces

symbols.name: Lstable
symbols.def: its Lévy measure is the pushforward of \(\Lambda\) by \((s,r,u)\mapsto r/s\)

symbols.name: sigmaHat
symbols.role: empirical standard deviation of the cross-fitted uncentered score

symbols.name: qfun
symbols.def: the left-continuous \(u\)-quantile of \(L_{\kappa,H,h_0}\), with the stable endpoint interpreted as \(S_{\alpha,H}\)

assumptions.condition: \(d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(\mathcal L_P\{(R,\tau(X))\mid A=1,e(X)\leq t\},H\right)\leq C_{\mathrm{mark}}t^{\rho}\) for every \(0<t\leq t_0\).

novel.justification: Joint convergence is realistic when the outcome regressions and treated residual law vary continuously at a smooth propensity boundary. The explicit \(C^2\) Bernoulli subclass below satisfies it with a deterministic boundary law and order \(t\) error.

Diverging odds multipliers formalize increasingly forceful encouragement policies and the approach from support-respecting IPSI toward near-universal treatment; this sequence is the scientific intervention regime rather than a proof device.
Polynomial boundary density is a concrete covariate model generating the stipulated weak-overlap tail; it includes beta-type densities and smooth perturbations used in applied propensity diagnostics.

A linearly vanishing propensity arises in threshold-crossing assignment models after a smooth boundary coordinate transformation and allows direct estimation of relative, rather than merely absolute, propensity error.

The restriction admits beta-like covariate densities, a broad open ball of smooth propensity factors, and nondegenerate Bernoulli regressions; it excludes only outcome and design degeneracy at the boundary.

definitions.name: Second-order marked weak-overlap class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{RV}}=\{P:(O_i)_{i=1}^n\text{ obey independent identical sampling, causal consistency, conditional exchangeability, bounded outcomes, one-sided support, }\kappa\in[\kappa_-,\kappa_+],\text{ the second-order lower-tail inequality, joint boundary-mark convergence, and residual separation}\}\) for every triangular index \(n\geq1\).

definitions.name: Primitive \(C^2\) boundary class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{C^2}=\{P:B\geq1,\ X\in[0,1],\ f_X(x)=x^{\kappa-1}\ell(x),\ \int_0^1x^{\kappa-1}\ell(x)dx=1,\ e(x)=xg(x),\ \ell,g,\mu_0,\mu_1\text{ obey the displayed }C^2\text{ and separation conditions, }\mathcal L_P(Y\mid A=a,X=x)=\operatorname{Bernoulli}[(1-a)\mu_0(x)+a\mu_1(x)]\text{ on support }\{0,1\}\subset[-B,B]\text{ for }a\in\{0,1\},\text{ and the displayed sampling and causal conditions hold}\}\) for every \(n\geq1\).

definitions.name: Equivalent-power hardening normalizer
definitions.construction: \(T(t)=E_P[e(X)\mathbf1\{e(X)\leq t\}],\ K=c\kappa/(1+\kappa),\ a_n=(nK)^{1/(1+\kappa)}\), and \(h_n=\delta_n/a_n\); an asymptotically equivalent generalized inverse satisfying \(nT(1/a_n)\to1\) is admissible.

definitions.name: Compensated critical marked law
definitions.construction: For \(h_0\in(0,\infty)\), \(L_{\kappa,H,h_0}\) is defined by \(\log E\exp(itL_{\kappa,H,h_0})=\int[\exp\{it g_{h_0}(s,r,u)\}-1-it g_{h_0}(s,r,u)]\alpha s^\kappa ds\,H(dr,du)\), where \(g_{h_0}(s,r,u)=h_0r/(1+h_0s)+h_0u/(1+h_0s)^2\).

definitions.name: Residual stable endpoint
definitions.construction: \(S_{\alpha,H}\) is the centered infinitely-divisible law obtained by pushing \(\alpha s^\kappa ds\,H(dr,du)\) through \((s,r,u)\mapsto r/s\); equivalently its positive and negative Lévy tails are \(x^{-\alpha}E_H[(R_+)^\alpha]\) and \(x^{-\alpha}E_H[(R_-)^\alpha]\).

definitions.name: Cross-fitted boundary local-linear one-step estimator
definitions.construction: Partition \([0,1]\) into bins of width \(b_n\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(5+\kappa_+)}\). On each training fold, estimate \(g\) from \(\sum X_iB_iB_i^{\mathsf T}\widehat\theta=\sum B_iA_i\), estimate \(\mu_1\) and \(\mu_0\) by treatment-weighted local linear least squares, clip to the primitive bounds, and set \(\widehat e(x)=x\widehat g(x)\). For held-out unit \(i\), write \(\widehat D_i=1+(\delta_n-1)\widehat e_i\) and define the uncentered fitted score \(\widehat\varphi_{\delta_n,i}=A_i\delta_n\{Y_i-\widehat\mu_{1,i}\}/\widehat D_i+(1-A_i)\{Y_i-\widehat\mu_{0,i}\}/\widehat D_i+\delta_n(\widehat\mu_{1,i}-\widehat\mu_{0,i})(A_i-\widehat e_i)/\widehat D_i^2+\widehat\mu_{0,i}+\delta_n\widehat e_i(\widehat\mu_{1,i}-\widehat\mu_{0,i})/\widehat D_i\), where every fitted value comes from the training fold excluding \(i\). Set \(\widehat\psi_{\delta_n}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat\varphi_{\delta_n,i}\).

definitions.name: Cross-fitted empirical score variance
definitions.construction: \(\widehat\sigma_n^2=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat\varphi_{\delta_n,i}-\widehat\psi_{\delta_n}\}^2\), with \(\widehat\varphi_{\delta_n,i}\) evaluated using the nuisance fits trained off the fold containing unit \(i\).

definitions.name: Empirical tail and joint-mark calibration
definitions.construction: With \(t_n=n^{-\beta}\), define \(\widehat T(t)=n^{-1}\sum_iA_i\mathbf1\{\widehat e_i\leq t\}\), \(\widehat\alpha=\log\{\widehat T(2t_n)/\widehat T(t_n)\}/\log2\), \(\widehat K=\widehat T(t_n)/t_n^{\widehat\alpha}\), \(\widehat a_n=(n\widehat K)^{1/\widehat\alpha}\), and \(\widehat H\) as the empirical law of \((Y_i-\widehat\mu_1(X_i),\widehat\mu_1(X_i)-\widehat\mu_0(X_i))\) among \(A_i=1\) and \(\widehat e_i\leq t_n\).

definitions.name: Separated-regime confidence intervals
definitions.construction: Let \(\widehat q\) be obtained by deterministic one-dimensional Fourier inversion of the plug-in Lévy exponent with certified total numerical error \(\epsilon_n^{\mathrm{inv}}\to0\). Set \(C_n^{\mathrm G}(\gamma)=[\widehat\psi_{\delta_n}\pm z_{1-\gamma/2}\widehat\sigma_n/\sqrt n]\), \(C_n^{\mathrm C}(\gamma)=[\widehat\psi_{\delta_n}-(\widehat a_n/n)\widehat q(1-\gamma/2),\widehat\psi_{\delta_n}-(\widehat a_n/n)\widehat q(\gamma/2)]\), and define \(C_n^{\mathrm S}(\gamma)\) by the same formula using the plug-in stable endpoint exponent.

definitions.name: Transition-experiment and ordered-modulus handle
definitions.construction: Start from the estimated hardening coordinate \(\widehat h_n\) and the fitted characteristic exponent, derive the joint local experiment when \(h_n\) approaches either branch boundary at the normalizer-estimation resolution, and compute the ordered modulus between adjacent tail and boundary-mark classes to choose a single calibrated acceptance region.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{RV}}\): if \(h_n\to0\), then \(\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\delta_n}(O_i)/(\sqrt n\sigma_n)\Rightarrow N(0,1)\); if \(h_n\to h_0\in(0,\infty)\), then \(a_n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\delta_n}(O_i)\Rightarrow L_{\kappa,H,h_0}\); and if \(h_n\to\infty\), then \(a_n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\delta_n}(O_i)\Rightarrow S_{\alpha,H}\). Uniformity is branchwise over compact parameter sets separated from the two transition boundaries. This is a strict multiplier-domain extension of Kennedy's fixed-compact Gaussian result because it includes diverging \(\delta_n\) and two non-Gaussian branches.
statements.justification: The theorem locates the exact stochastic frontier at which a positivity-robust incremental mean acquires weak-overlap non-Gaussian uncertainty.
statements.gap: Kennedy2019Incremental stops at fixed compact multipliers, while MaWang2020RobustIPW varies trimming for a fixed target and therefore has neither the moving centering nor the IPSI contrast mark.
statements.consumer: It determines when the Gaussian approximation in \(\mathtt{npcausal::ipsi}\) must be replaced as analysts extend odds shifts beyond a bounded range.

statements.statement: For every \(h_0\in(0,\infty)\), the absolute \(\Lambda\)-mass of the propensity-path component is \(\int |h_0u/(1+h_0s)^2|\,d\Lambda=\alpha\operatorname{Beta}(1+\kappa,1-\kappa)E_H|u|\,h_0^{-\kappa}\). Hence this component is absent at a finite critical coordinate if and only if \(u=0\) \(H\)-almost surely; if \(E_H|u|>0\), it remains strictly positive for every finite \(h_0\) and vanishes only at the stable endpoint \(h_0\to\infty\). Moreover \(\int|g_{h_0}(s,r,u)-r/s|\,d\Lambda=O(h_0^{-\kappa})\).
statements.justification: This prevents invalid residual-only critical calibration and identifies precisely when the extra causal-policy mark can be ignored.
statements.gap: Neither Kennedy2019Incremental nor the scalar boundary laws in MaWang2020RobustIPW characterize equality of these marked Lévy pushforwards.
statements.consumer: Software can use the criterion to decide whether a simpler stable-mark approximation is legitimate at a finite hardening coordinate.

statements.statement: Under the declared primitive envelope \(B\geq1\), the conditional Bernoulli support \(\{0,1\}\) lies in \([-B,B]\). There exist common \(c_-\), \(c_+\), \(\underline t\), \(C_{\mathrm{tail}}\), \(C_{\mathrm{mark}}\), and \(v_*\), depending only on the primitive class constants, such that every \(P\in\mathcal P_{C^2}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{RV}}\), with \(c=\ell(0)/\{\kappa g(0)^\kappa\}\), second-order exponent \(\rho=1\), and \(H\) equal to the boundary law of the Bernoulli treated residual paired with \(\mu_1(0)-\mu_0(0)\).
statements.justification: The inclusion proves that the explicit feasible model is nonempty and genuinely instantiates the marked regular-variation class rather than assuming membership.
statements.gap: The published weak-overlap papers impose tail conditions directly; they do not derive the required joint IPSI boundary mark from a primitive nonparametric covariate model.
statements.consumer: The proposition makes the early learner and calibration tests executable on a transparent beta-type design with binary outcomes.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{C^2}\), the local-linear construction satisfies \(\|\widehat e/e-1\|_\infty+\|\widehat\mu_0-\mu_0\|_\infty+\|\widehat\mu_1-\mu_1\|_\infty=O_P(r_n)\), with \(r_n=(\log n/n)^{2/(5+\kappa_+)}\), and its centered fitted score differs from the centered oracle score by \(o_P(\sigma_n/\sqrt n)\) when \(h_n\to0\) and by \(o_P(a_n/n)\) when \(h_n\) is bounded away from zero, including \(h_n\to\infty\). On every separated Gaussian sequence \(h_n\leq\eta_n\to0\), the explicit empirical score variance satisfies \(\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n\to_P1\). Consequently \(\widehat\psi_{\delta_n}\) inherits every branch of Theorem 1 without an assumed final remainder.
statements.justification: The result turns the point-process law into a feasible nonparametric estimator and supplies the early kill test for the proposal.
statements.gap: Ordinary DML controls fixed finite-variance scores in unweighted \(L_2\) norms; HiranoImbensRidder2003 and MaWang2020RobustIPW use regular or parametric first steps rather than relative-error boundary learning.
statements.consumer: It gives a checkable learner implementation for the binary nuMoM2b outcome and a reference path for extending \(\mathtt{npcausal::ipsi}\).

statements.statement: Choose \(t_n=n^{-\beta}\) so that \(nT(t_n)\to\infty\) and \(\log n\{r_n+t_n^\rho+[nT(t_n)]^{-1/2}\}\to0\). Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{C^2}\), the empirical calibration obeys \(\widehat a_n/a_n\to_P1\) and \(d_{\mathrm{BL}}(\widehat H,H)\to_P0\). If \(h_n\leq\eta_n\to0\), then the cross-fitted empirical variance obeys \(\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n\to_P1\) and \(P\{\psi_{\delta_n}\in C_n^{\mathrm G}(\gamma)\}=1-\gamma+o(1)\); if \(h_n\in[h_-,h_+]\subset(0,\infty)\), then \(P\{\psi_{\delta_n}\in C_n^{\mathrm C}(\gamma)\}=1-\gamma+o(1)\); and if \(h_n\geq M_n\to\infty\), then \(P\{\psi_{\delta_n}\in C_n^{\mathrm S}(\gamma)\}=1-\gamma+o(1)\). Each remainder is uniform within its stated separated branch and includes score replacement, variance estimation in the Gaussian branch, tail and mark estimation, normalizer error, anti-concentration, and certified inversion error. The critical branch strictly extends Kennedy's multiplier-bootstrap coverage beyond a fixed compact multiplier set.
statements.justification: This is the publishable inferential kernel: a non-Gaussian hardening limit is operational only when its unknown asymmetric quantiles can be estimated with honest coverage.
statements.gap: Kennedy2019Incremental covers fixed-index Gaussian processes; HeilerKazak2021Irregular and MaWang2020RobustIPW calibrate fixed causal targets without a two-component estimated boundary mark or moving-target normalizer.
statements.consumer: The result supplies regime-valid uncertainty for harder odds shifts in the Naimi et al. vegetable--preeclampsia analysis while leaving its reported bounded-range conclusions untouched.

statements.statement: Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{RV}}\) and a sequence with \(h_n\to0\). Along the dominated local paths \(dP_{n,u}/dP=1+u\phi_{\delta_n}/(\sqrt n\sigma_n)\), uniformly for \(u\) in compact sets, the log-likelihood ratio is \(u\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\delta_n}(O_i)/(\sqrt n\sigma_n)-u^2/2+o_P(1)\) and \(\sqrt n\{\psi_{\delta_n}(P_{n,u})-\psi_{\delta_n}(P)\}/\sigma_n=u+o(1)\). Oracle pointwise bound over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{RV}}\): every estimator regular in this ambient triangular experiment has a convolution factor \(N(0,1)\), and the oracle one-step estimator \(\widetilde\psi_{\delta_n}\) attains the bound. Feasible attainment on \(\mathcal P_{C^2}\): if in addition \(P\in\mathcal P_{C^2}\), then the cross-fitted estimator \(\widehat\psi_{\delta_n}\) is regular in the same pointwise experiment and attains the bound.
statements.justification: A moving functional requires its own local experiment; the result certifies that the Gaussian normalization is an efficiency frontier rather than a convenient CLT scale.
statements.gap: Kennedy2019Incremental gives a fixed-functional efficiency bound, and KhanTamer2010Irregular diagnoses inverse-weight irregularity without a drifting IPSI tangent experiment.
statements.consumer: It provides the benchmark against which alternative regular estimators for moderate but increasing odds shifts can be compared.

statements.statement: If \(\delta_n\equiv\delta_0\in(0,\infty)\) and \(E_P[\phi_{\delta_0}(O)^2]\in(0,\infty)\), then the target and score reduce to Kennedy's point-treatment incremental mean and efficient influence function, and the Gaussian interval reduces to the pointwise version of Kennedy's fixed-compact multiplier procedure.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check and prevents the hardening theory from changing the established estimand at ordinary multipliers.
statements.gap: This is a compatibility corollary rather than a novelty claim; it pins the new notation to Kennedy2019Incremental exactly.
statements.consumer: Existing bounded-multiplier analyses retain their familiar pointwise Gaussian interpretation.

statements.statement: Can a single data-driven confidence set based on the transition-experiment and ordered-modulus handle cover \(\psi_{\delta_n}\) uniformly over local sequences approaching both hardening boundaries, with oracle-order expected length on each separated branch; or must every honest procedure pay a logarithmic length factor determined by simultaneous uncertainty in \(\kappa\), \(\rho\), and \(H\)?
statements.justification: Separated-regime validity does not answer what an analyst should do when the estimated normalizer places the multiplier near a transition.
statements.gap: HeilerKazak2021Irregular adapts between regular and stable laws for a fixed target, whereas this problem has two transitions, a moving target, and an intermediate marked family.
statements.consumer: A resolution would permit one automatic hardening diagnostic and interval in software without user-supplied regime labels.

sampling_model.design: Independent identical superpopulation sampling under \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{RV}}\), with feasible results on \(\mathcal P_{C^2}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with \(P(A=1\mid X)=e(X)\) and a deterministic incremental odds multiplier \(\delta_n\to\infty\).
sampling_model.overlap: One-sided weak support with \(P\{e(X)\leq t\}=ct^\kappa\{1+O(t^\rho)\}\), where \(0<\kappa_-\leq\kappa\leq\kappa_+<1\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold cross-fitted boundary local-linear estimates of \(g\), \(\mu_0\), and \(\mu_1\), an empirical variance of the held-out fitted uncentered scores, and empirical tail and joint-mark calibration.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat\psi_{\delta_n}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat\varphi_{\delta_n,-k(i)}(O_i)\), with branch scale \(\sqrt n/\widehat\sigma_n\) or \(n/\widehat a_n\) according to \(\widehat h_n=\delta_n/\widehat a_n\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The estimator converges in distribution to a Gaussian process on a bounded multiplier set.
Under moderate trimming the asymptotic distribution is infinitely divisible.
Treatment effect parameter estimates converge in distribution to alpha-stable random variables.
The DML estimators are approximately linear and centered Gaussian.
The best possible root mean squared error scales with an effective sample size of \(n/\delta\).
Tail trimming with estimated bias produces asymptotically normal inference under limited overlap.

tldr: Binary incremental propensity interventions avoid a fixed positivity condition only while their odds multiplier remains moderate. On a second-order regularly varying lower-propensity class, the cross-fitted incremental-mean score instead has a hardening frontier indexed by \(h_n=\delta_n/a_n\): a Gaussian law below the frontier, a compensated marked infinitely-divisible law at it, and a residual stable law above it. The critical jump retains both the treated outcome residual and the propensity-path treatment contrast. The project derives these laws, proves oracle replacement and relative consistency of an explicit cross-fitted score-variance estimator on a nonparametric \(C^2\) class, estimates the tail normalizer and joint boundary marks, certifies numerical Lévy inversion, and establishes branchwise uniform coverage. The Gaussian branch carries an oracle ambient pointwise convolution bound over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{RV}}\), with feasible attainment asserted only on \(\mathcal P_{C^2}\).

project_justification.gap: Published IPSI inference holds over fixed compact multiplier sets, while published weak-overlap stable and infinitely-divisible results concern fixed inverse-weight targets or externally trimmed scores. Neither literature handles a moving binary incremental target whose score itself changes at the rare-treatment scale.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a feasible marked-law calibration theorem: the finite-positive branch depends jointly on a residual mark and a policy-path contrast, and both its normalizer and its asymmetric quantiles must be estimated near an unknown propensity boundary.
project_justification.fill: The paper constructs the three-regime law, a concrete cross-fitted boundary learner, an explicit empirical variance of held-out fitted scores, empirical tail and joint-mark estimates, and confidence intervals whose uniform coverage includes nuisance and variance replacement, logarithmic normalizer sensitivity, anti-concentration, and deterministic inversion error.

related_work: Kennedy2019Incremental supplies the exact incremental estimand, its propensity-dependent efficient influence function, and Gaussian-process inference on bounded multiplier sets; Theorem 3 strictly enlarges that coverage domain to diverging multipliers in separated regimes, while Theorem 4 gives the distinct ambient pointwise efficiency statement. MaWang2020RobustIPW supplies the regular-variation and compensation template for trimmed fixed-target inverse weighting, but its scalar boundary mark cannot represent the IPSI propensity-path contrast. HeilerKazak2021Irregular establishes stable causal-score limits and warns that the ordinary bootstrap fails, informing the direct non-Gaussian calibration in Theorem 3. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML provides the foldwise orthogonal expansion rebuilt in tail-weighted and truncated norms in Theorem 2. HiranoImbensRidder2003 motivates the concrete growing-local-basis propensity fit, while the boundary information calculation targets relative error. SchindlShenKennedy2026Continuous shows that unbounded tilts matter for continuous exposures, but its effective-sample-size and edge-dose analysis has a different localization mechanism. NaimiEtAl2021TimeFixed provides the writing and application exemplar: its nuMoM2b analysis uses odds multipliers from \(0.20\) to \(5.0\), and Theorem 3 governs extensions toward increasingly forceful odds shifts rather than revising that bounded-range analysis.
technical_internal_limitation: The branchwise theorem deliberately excludes automatic classification on local sequences at the two transition boundaries. The critical Lévy inversion must carry deterministic quadrature, frequency-truncation, spatial-tail, and aliasing certificates; numerical grid stability alone is not counted as proof. Theorem 4 is pointwise in the full dominated observed-law experiment: its oracle convolution bound applies over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{RV}}\), its feasible-attainment clause applies only at base laws in \(\mathcal P_{C^2}\), and neither clause is a minimax claim within the smaller \(C^2\) tail class.
honest_scope: The oracle jump map, score-bias algebra, hard-endpoint reduction, local-linear rate route, empirical score-variance route, and smoothing inequality are verified presolve evidence, not established results. The main open proof is Theorem 3: uniform plug-in quantile coverage after score and variance replacement, random tail-shell estimation, logarithmically sensitive normalizer calibration, joint-mark estimation, and certified inversion. Theorem 4 gives an oracle pointwise ambient convolution bound over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{RV}}\); feasible attainment is limited to \(\mathcal P_{C^2}\). The fully adaptive transition problem remains Open-ended Question 1. Fixed multipliers reduce to Kennedy's result, and neither endpoint \(\kappa=0\) nor \(\kappa=1\), unbounded outcomes, longitudinal treatment, or simultaneous bands over an unbounded multiplier curve are claimed.

seed_details.title: Feasible marked-Lévy quantiles for hardening binary incremental means
seed_details.anchor: Kennedy2019Incremental, Theorems 3--4 and Appendix Sections 8.4--8.5; MaWang2020RobustIPW, Theorem 1 and Section 3.3; HeilerKazak2021Irregular, accepted-manuscript sections on stable limits and adaptive inference
seed_details.proof_boundary: Kennedy's multiplier coupling uses a Lipschitz score class on a fixed compact multiplier set. The first changed step is the bounded-envelope empirical-process approximation: when \(\delta_n\) diverges, its replacement is tail-weighted score coupling plus estimation of an asymmetric marked Lévy exponent.
seed_details.destination_search: Exact searches for binary incremental propensity interventions combined with diverging multipliers, regular variation, stable limits, or marked-Lévy inversion returned fixed-index IPSI, fixed-target IPW, and continuous-exposure tilts, but no binary hardening coverage theorem.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee will call this Ma and Wang's regime-robust IPW inference with Kennedy's score substituted.
seed_details.rebuttal: The critical jump is not the fixed-target IPW mark: it jointly contains the treated residual and the derivative of a propensity-dependent moving intervention, while feasible calibration must estimate that joint boundary mark and a logarithmically sensitive normalizer.

seed_details.title: Gaussian, marked infinitely-divisible, and stable limits along the binary IPSI hardening scale
seed_details.anchor: Kennedy2019Incremental, Corollary 1 and Theorem 2; MaWang2020RobustIPW, Lemma 1 and Theorem 1
seed_details.proof_boundary: Kennedy's point-treatment score is finite-variance for each fixed multiplier, while Ma and Wang vary an external trimming threshold for a fixed target. The first changed step is triangular marked-point-process convergence for a score whose target and propensity derivative both move with \(\delta_n\).
seed_details.destination_search: The binary IPSI plus regular-variation search found no paper deriving a finite-positive hardening law with a two-coordinate boundary mark.
seed_details.red_team: The three regimes are immediate from standard point-process theory and Ma and Wang's Theorem 1.
seed_details.rebuttal: Standard machinery does not determine the changing IPSI jump map, its compensation, or the contrast term that remains first order at finite positive \(h\).

seed_details.title: Necessary and sufficient disappearance of the propensity-path contrast mark
seed_details.proof_boundary: Kennedy's chain-rule calculation creates the propensity-path score term. The first changed step is to push that term through the lower-propensity point process and characterize exactly when its Lévy measure contribution is zero.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for propensity-path marks or contrast extinction in incremental-effect stable laws returned no matching result.
seed_details.red_team: The contrast disappears by inspection after sending \(h\) to infinity.
seed_details.rebuttal: Endpoint disappearance is easy, but necessity at every finite positive \(h\) is a statement about equality of Lévy measures and rules out residual-only critical calibration except under boundary contrast degeneracy.

seed_details.title: Pointwise convolution bound for the drifting IPSI functional in the Gaussian branch
seed_details.anchor: Kennedy2019Incremental, Theorem 2; KhanTamer2010Irregular, treatment-effect support example
seed_details.proof_boundary: Substitution of \(\delta_n\) into a fixed-functional efficiency bound is invalid. The first changed step is to verify quadratic-mean differentiability and the moving target derivative on a least-favorable triangular path.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for triangular LAN or convolution bounds for diverging binary incremental odds multipliers found continuous-treatment tilt bounds but no binary weak-overlap experiment.
seed_details.red_team: Kennedy's efficient influence function already gives the bound after replacing \(\delta\) by \(\delta_n\).
seed_details.rebuttal: A drifting derivative and diverging score variance require an explicit triangular likelihood expansion; fixed-parameter pathwise differentiability alone does not imply a convolution theorem.

seed_details.title: Necessary and sufficient tail-band learner conditions for oracle replacement
seed_details.anchor: ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A.12; Kennedy2019Incremental, Theorem 3 and Appendix 8.4
seed_details.proof_boundary: DML conditions control ordinary \(L_2(P)\) products and Kennedy uses a bounded multiplier set. The first changed step is foldwise conditioning in the moving singular norm generated near \(e(X)\asymp a_n^{-1}\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for cross-fitted IPSI under regular variation found fixed-index DML and parametric estimated-weight stable theory, but not a nonparametric relative-error learner theorem across all hardening regimes.
seed_details.red_team: This is an ordinary DML product-rate proof with weighted norms.
seed_details.rebuttal: The hard branch has no finite second moment and requires truncated-tail replacement rather than an \(L_2\) argument; a converse learner frontier is not supplied by DML.
seed_details.decision: survives as a secondary candidate; the sufficient concrete \(C^2\) route is incorporated and the converse is deferred

seed_details.title: Honest adaptation across both hardening transitions and unknown tail smoothness
seed_details.anchor: HeilerKazak2021Irregular, accepted-manuscript sections on adaptive inference and implementation; MaWang2020RobustIPW, Section 3.3
seed_details.proof_boundary: Existing adaptation holds a causal target fixed. The first changed step is regime classification when \(h_n=\delta_n/a_n\) itself uses an estimated tail inverse and has nonvanishing error on local transition sequences.
seed_details.destination_search: No located procedure adapts simultaneously to a drifting binary IPSI score, an intermediate marked law, and second-order tail uncertainty.
seed_details.red_team: One can pretest \(h_n\) and select among the three branchwise intervals.
seed_details.rebuttal: Local sequences near either boundary make pretest error first order; honest adaptation requires a new transition experiment or an ordered-modulus lower bound.
seed_details.decision: survives only as the first-class open-ended question

seed_details.title: Equivalence frontier for retuned \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) hardening resampling
seed_details.anchor: HeilerKazak2021Irregular, accepted-manuscript adaptive-resampling section; MaWang2020RobustIPW, Algorithm 2
seed_details.proof_boundary: Resampling at the original multiplier changes the critical coordinate. The first changed step is to transport the moving target and set \(\delta_m=\delta_n(m/n)^{1/\alpha}\) while controlling tail-index error times \(\lvert\log(m/n)\rvert\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found adaptive \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) inference for fixed treatment effects, but not resampling that preserves a moving incremental target's critical coordinate.
seed_details.red_team: Retuning the multiplier is a one-line scaling correction to Heiler and Kazak.
seed_details.rebuttal: The resample must also re-center a different causal target and preserve a two-component marked law under estimated \(\alpha\); these are first-order operations at the critical scale.
seed_details.decision: survives but is not selected because direct Lévy calibration has cleaner feasibility

seed_details.title: Weak-overlap regret for choosing an incremental odds multiplier
seed_details.anchor: Kennedy2019Incremental, Discussion, especially the displayed optimal incremental regime
seed_details.proof_boundary: The destination would replace estimation of a fixed \(\delta\) by empirical maximization over a growing multiplier class. The first changed step is uniform value control over \(\delta\leq\Delta_n\).
seed_details.destination_search: The search found a public positivity-free policy-learning manuscript that already studies incremental propensity-score policy classes, while the scalar multiplier problem risks an endpoint optimum without an added welfare cost.
seed_details.red_team: Without a substantively justified intervention cost, welfare is often monotone in the scalar multiplier and the policy problem is vacuous; related positivity-free policy learning is already public.
seed_details.rebuttal: No non-artificial cost or nondegenerate scalar decision frontier was found in the topic substrate.

seed_details.title: Permutation inversion for hardening incremental means
seed_details.anchor: HeilerKazak2021Irregular, Section 4 on resampling failure and repair
seed_details.proof_boundary: An M17 route would require an exact or approximately valid orbit for the causal score. The first changed step is constructing that orbit under observational exchangeability.
seed_details.destination_search: No assignment group, placebo panel, or block-exchangeable residual structure is supplied by the iid observational model.
seed_details.red_team: Conditional exchangeability identifies the target but does not create the finite-sample symmetry needed for conformal or permutation validity.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds without adding a randomized design or an artificial residual-symmetry model.

threads: Kennedy2019Incremental proves an efficient score, cross-fitted weak convergence, and multiplier-bootstrap coverage only on a fixed compact multiplier set; Appendix 8.4 relies on a Lipschitz envelope bounded through the lower endpoint of that set.

MaWang2020RobustIPW uses regular variation, bias correction, and subsampling for a fixed IPW target across trimming regimes; its Theorem 1 supplies the nearest infinitely-divisible construction but not a propensity-dependent moving target or joint boundary mark.
HeilerKazak2021Irregular obtains stable IPW and doubly robust limits and an adaptive \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap; its first steps are parametric and its law has no finite-positive hardening mark.
HillChaudhuri2025HeavyTail trims the realized feasible IPW score and bias-corrects it toward Gaussianity; it neither estimates a marked Lévy law nor studies IPSI.
literature_map.subsumption_check: No thread supplies uniform plug-in quantiles for the binary moving incremental mean. The nearest 2026 diverging-tilt paper, SchindlShenKennedy2026Continuous, treats continuous exposures and minimax rates rather than the binary weak-overlap marked phase transition.

threads: Kennedy2019Incremental, Corollary 1 identifies the same point-treatment mean and Theorem 2 derives the propensity-path component of its efficient influence function.
MaWang2020RobustIPW, Lemma 1 pushes a conditional boundary law through an inverse weight and Theorem 1 derives Gaussian and infinitely-divisible trimming regimes.
BonviniEtAl2021Review surveys binary incremental effects, estimation, and positivity advantages without diverging-multiplier asymptotics.

SchindlShenKennedy2026Continuous permits an unbounded exponential tilt for a continuous exposure and derives an effective sample size, but its boundary localization and score are not the rare-treated binary mechanism.
literature_map.subsumption_check: The exact binary target--method pair remains unoccupied. In particular, no located source has the jump \(h r/(1+hs)+h u/(1+hs)^2\) or proves that only its second component disappears as \(h\to\infty\).

threads: ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML proves centered Gaussian linearization from orthogonality and cross-fitting under ordinary moment and product-rate conditions; Appendix A.12 conditions on folds and then applies Lindeberg--Feller.
Kennedy2019Incremental derives the exact IPSI score remainder on a fixed multiplier domain.
HiranoImbensRidder2003 proves efficiency for inverse weighting with a fitted growing-series propensity under regular overlap.
MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2023WeakOverlap combines trimming with bias correction for a fixed target rather than replacing a moving, untrimmed IPSI score.
literature_map.subsumption_check: These results do not prove relative propensity error down to \(e(X)\asymp a_n^{-1}\), the truncated-tail replacement needed when the score lacks a second moment, or empirical boundary-mark consistency with generated propensity coordinates.

novelty_justification: The closest target-side result is Kennedy2019Incremental: its Theorems 3--4 give Gaussian-process and multiplier-bootstrap inference for \(\delta\) in a fixed compact subset of \((0,\infty)\). The closest probability-side result is MaWang2020RobustIPW: its Theorem 1 varies trimming for a fixed inverse-weight target. The proposed kernel changes both sides simultaneously. The causal target \(\psi_{\delta_n}\) moves, the efficient score contains the propensity-path contrast inherited from Kennedy's Lemma 4, and the critical Lévy measure is the pushforward of a joint treated boundary mark rather than the scalar fixed-target mark in Ma and Wang. No located paper proves feasible, uniform quantile coverage after nonparametric score replacement, generalized-inverse tail calibration, joint-mark estimation, and certified inversion. The continuous-exposure tilt theory of Schindl, Shen, and Kennedy confirms that unbounded tilts can alter rates, but it does not subsume the binary rare-treatment point process or its stable endpoint.
